post.description: Returns a short-lived access token and sets the refresh token as an httpOnly cookie: __Host-refresh_token on Path=/ in production (Secure), refresh_token scoped to /api/auth elsewhere. A session this browser already had is ended.
post.summary: Sign in with email and password

post.description: Reads the refresh cookie (__Host-refresh_token in production, refresh_token elsewhere). Each refresh token works once; presenting one that was rotated more than 30 seconds ago ends its whole session family.
post.summary: Rotate the refresh cookie and mint a new access token

post.description: Without sessionIds, ends the refresh cookie's session, whichever it is. With them, ends it only when it is one of those sessions (AuthSession.sessionId), and clears the cookies only then; a live session started meanwhile is left alone, with its session hint set again.
post.summary: End the current session family and clear the cookies

get.summary: What this deployment offers: password recovery, public sign-up, change of email, invitations

post.description: Answers 202 for any well-formed request whose password follows the policy. A new address gets a one-time link (valid 24 hours) to confirm it; one that already has an account gets a notice to its owner instead. No account exists until the link is confirmed. 400: the password is refused (too short, too common, too easy to guess, or containing the email or name). 403: sign-up is closed here.
post.summary: Sign up: ask for a confirmation link

post.description: Creates the account and signs it in, like a sign-in (refresh cookie, access token). 401: not the password chosen at sign-up (a few wrong ones drop the sign-up). 403: sign-up is closed here. 404: the link is invalid, replaced, used or expired. 409: the address got an account meanwhile.
post.summary: Confirm a sign-up with its link's token and its password

post.description: Answers 204 for any well-formed address. If it has an account, a message with a one-time link (valid 30 minutes) is on its way. 503 when this deployment sends no email.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset link

post.description: The token works once. Every session of the account ends; nobody is signed in. 400: the new password is refused (too short, too common, too easy to guess, or containing the email or name), the link still works. 404: the link is invalid, used or expired.
post.summary: Choose a new password with a reset link's token

post.description: Every other session ends; this browser gets a new session (a new access token in the body and a new refresh cookie). 400: the new password is refused (too short, too common, too easy to guess, or containing the email or name). 403: the current password is wrong. 409: the password changed meanwhile.
post.summary: Change the password, confirming the current one

post.description: Answers 202 once the current password is checked: a one-time link (valid 24 hours) goes to the new address, which changes only when it is opened; if the new address already has an account, its owner gets a notice instead. 400: the new address is the current one. 403: the current password is wrong. 503: this deployment sends no email.
post.summary: Ask to change the email address, confirming the current password

post.description: The token works once, while the account is as it was when the link was sent. The address changes, every session ends (sign in again with the new address), and the previous address gets a notice with a link to undo it. 404: the link is invalid, used or expired. 409: the new address got an account meanwhile.
post.summary: Confirm a new email address with the link sent to it

post.description: The token works once, for 7 days, whatever happened to the account since. The previous address comes back with the new password given here, and every session ends. 400: the password is refused (too short, too common, too easy to guess, or containing the email or name); the link still works. 404: the link is invalid, used or expired. 409: the previous address got another account meanwhile.
post.summary: Undo a change of email with the link sent to the previous address

post.description: Sends a one-time link (valid 7 days); the account exists once it is accepted with a name and a password the person chooses. Inviting an address again replaces its invitation and link. 409: the address has an account. 429: the address got a message moments ago (or several today). 503: this deployment sends no email.
post.summary: Invite an address to create an account with a role

delete.summary: Revoke an invitation: its link stops working at once

post.description: Creates the account with the invitation's role and signs it in, like a sign-in (refresh cookie, access token). 400: the password is refused (too short, too common, too easy to guess, or containing the email or name); the link still works. 404: the invitation is invalid, replaced, revoked, used or expired. 409: the address got an account meanwhile.
post.summary: Accept an invitation with its link's token, choosing a name and a password

get.description: Members may read only themselves; any other id answers 404. Admins read any.

get.summary: Liveness: the process is up (restart it when this fails)
Readiness: dependencies are reachable (route traffic only while this passes)

post.description: Sent by the web app when the page is hidden. Recorded as metrics by route pattern, metric, rating and navigation type (docs/observability.md#web-vitals); answered 204 also when metrics are off.
post.summary: Report the Web Vitals of a page load

info.title: API
info.description: REST API under /api. Every response body is { data, message }; errors carry data: null. Authenticated routes take the access token from POST /api/auth/sign-in as a bearer token; the refresh token is an httpOnly cookie.
